articleSummary: Mayaro virus, an enveloped positive-sense RNA alphavirus causing Mayaro fever with prolonged arthralgia, shows strong translational selection shaping codon usage across 91 complete coding sequences. The overall genome GC content is ~51%, with higher GC in the structural polyprotein and distinct pressures between structural and non-structural regions.

articleSummary: Dengue presents with fever, severe headache, pain behind the eyes, muscle and joint pains, and bone pain—often called bone-breaking fever. After fever subsides, risk remains for 2–3 days. Do not take aspirin or ibuprofen during fever. Do not let water stagnate in any household container—tanks, pots, coolers, packets, diapers, coconut cups, bottles, or plastic cups—and clean storage weekly. Dengue mosquitoes breed in clean water and bite mainly during the day; use mosquito nets, wear covered clothing, and install screens. Keep children under mosquito nets during the day. If fever persists beyond 2 days, seek testing at a government hospital and stay hydrated with fluids or ORS, unless advised otherwise.

articleSummary: In Belo Horizonte, Brazil, the four-year EVITA trial released millions of Aedes aegypti mosquitoes infected with Wolbachia pipientis strain mWel across 58 districts (29 treated, 29 control) to curb dengue, Zika, and chikungunya transmission. The study enrolled 3,480 children aged 6–11 and monitored arboviral infections via blood tests. Wolbachia in mosquitoes suppresses replication of several viruses and reduces mosquito reproduction; it is maternally transmitted, enabling local spread through the population. Results, presented at the American Society for Tropical Medicine and Hygiene meeting in late November and pending peer-reviewed publication, show an overall arboviral infection reduction of 68.6%, dengue infections down 68.5%, and chikungunya down 73.3%. The approach does not eradicate mosquitoes but lowers transmission risk; it could be scalable for up to four billion people in dengue-endemic regions. Emory led the project; Yale’s Albert Ko highlighted its potential as a sustainable preventive tool.

articleSummary: Uncontrolled blood glucose increases infection risk in diabetes, illustrated by a 60-year-old woman in Ho Chi Minh City whose diabetes worsened after a herpes zoster (shingles) outbreak on the chest. Although skin lesions improved, persistent neuralgia disrupted sleep and daily life, complicating glucose control. Endocrinology experts warn that infections such as influenza, pneumonia, respiratory syncytial virus (RSV), and herpes zoster can have amplified effects in older adults with multiple chronic diseases. Infections can impair immune function and destabilize glycemic management, occasionally requiring hospitalization. Preventing infections should be an integral part of diabetes care, alongside glycemic control, weight management, and nutrition. Recommendations include vaccination tailored to age and comorbidity, and discussing infection risks and preventive measures at each follow-up visit.

articleHeadline: Urban Contaminants Drive Mosquito Metabolic Adaptation and Public Health
articleSummary: Urban contaminants in Sub-Saharan Africa are reshaping malaria vector (Anopheles) larval environments, prompting metabolic adaptations that undercut insecticide efficacy. A narrative review of ecological, toxicological, and genomic evidence shows continual exposure to heavy metals, petroleum hydrocarbons, detergents, pesticides, and pharmaceutical residues driving metabolic pre-sensitization and multi-enzyme detox systems, yielding cross-resistance before adult vectors encounter treated nets. Across Lagos and Accra, upregulation of GSTe2, CYP6P3, and PPP enzymes; Yaoundé linked knockdown resistance mutations, ABC transporters, and cuticular hydrocarbons; Dar es Salaam and Kenyan sites show CYP6M2 upregulation with KDR alleles; Dakar and Ouagadougou associate with metabolic rate suppression; Lusaka, Ndola, Blantyre tie to altered lethal exposure thresholds. Urban farming in Cotonou/Porto-Novo and industrial zones in Yaoundé yield higher oxidase and GST activity. In controlled experiments with Anopheles arabiensis, cadmium, lead, and copper raise tolerance in resistant SENN DDT strains.

articleHeadline: Study Maps 28 Years of Pediatric Norovirus Research Across Global Networks
articleSummary: Global pediatric norovirus research has shifted from taxonomic identification to genomic tracking, burden quantification, and vaccine design from 1998–2025. Norovirus is a leading cause of acute gastroenteritis and diarrheal outbreaks worldwide, with more than 700 million infections and about 200,000 deaths annually; children under five bear the highest incidence and mortality. It accounts for roughly 63.20% of foodborne viral infections, transmitted primarily via fecal-oral routes through contaminated water, shellfish, produce, and ready-to-eat foods. No antiviral medications or approved vaccines exist. A bibliometric analysis of 2,161 English-language articles from Web of Science (1998–2025) shows three growth stages, peaking in 2021 with 150 papers. The United States leads with 406 publications, followed by China (307) and Japan (193). Leading institutions include University of Tokyo (84), Emory University (66), and Chiang Mai University (62); Baylor College of Medicine has the most citations. International collaboration remains strongest for the United States.

articleSummary: Dengue imported infections threaten non-endemic temperate countries Japan and the Republic of Korea, where annual imported cases can spark local transmission when Aedes aegypti or Aedes albopictus are present. It shows environmental signals reduce prediction error and enhance directional accuracy for imported dengue risk in Japan and Korea, outperforming trend-only models. articleHeadline: Spleen Imaging Accurately Predicts Esophageal Varices in Schistosomiasis
articleSummary: Spleen imaging accurately predicts esophageal varices in schistosomiasis-associated non-cirrhotic portal hypertension. In northeastern Brazil (Pernambuco), a prospective cross-sectional study of 71 consecutive patients with hepatosplenic schistosomiasis and advanced periportal fibrosis demonstrated that spleen-focused ultrasound parameters and spleen stiffness measured by point shear-wave elastography reliably identified varices, outperforming liver-based assessments. The team measured portal vein diameter, splenic vein diameter, and splenic dimensions to compute a splenic index, and assessed tissue stiffness with elastography on a Siemens Acuson S2000. A single blinded sonographer performed all exams. The cohort had median age 57; 77.5% were hepatosplenic form; 76.1% Niamey grade E/F fibrosis; 35.2% with prior upper GI bleeding. Findings support non-invasive spleen metrics—spleen stiffness, splenic vein diameter, and the splenic index—as potential risk-stratification tools, reducing dependence on invasive endoscopy in resource-constrained endemic centers.
